newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Orogen takes 20 pct of pipeline group.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Orogen takes 20 pct of pipeline group.

text.p: Orogen Minerals Ltd said on Monday it has taken a 20 percent interest in a consortium to study the feasibility of constructing a A$2 billion gas pipeline from Papua New Guinea to north Queensland.
The consortium would investigate the viability of producing gas in Papua New Guinea and delivering it to northern and central Queensland, said Orogen deputy chairman Lindsay MacAlister.
"Orogen has taken a 20 percent front-end interest in this consortium effort," MacAlister told a media briefing.
Orogen was also involved in a consortium which is seeking to market the gas, talking to potential end-users such as aluminum producer Comalco Ltd.
The pipeline consortium also comprised Chevron Corp unit Chevron Niugini Pty Ltd, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd unit BHP Petroleum (PNG) Inc, Oil Search Ltd and Mitsubishi unit Merlin Petroleum Co.
The consortium hopes to begin first deliveries of gas to Queensland by 2001.
MacAlister said Orogen expected to be involved with the pipeline section from the Kutubu oil and gas fields to the Papua New Guinea, estimated at about A$300 million.
The offshore and Australian element would be open to a consortium of parties, he said.
Chevron subsidiary Chevron South Pacific Co is developing the PNG/Queensland gas project consisting of gas production and LPG extraction along with processing facilities.
Orogen managing director Charles Lepani said the consortium was looking at a five-year window of opportunity to develop gas sales before other projects came onstream.
A gas pipeline would also boost oil production at the Kutubu project, as gas produced at Kutubu cannot by flared off under PNG law and was currently pumped back underground.
Kutubu partner Oil Search had estimated gas sales would increase oil production at the field by 20-25 million barrels.
Orogen, which holds the resources assets of the PNG government, earlier released its maiden results for the eight months to December 31, 1996.
Revenue came only from the four months from September 1.
Orogen said it recorded a net profit of kina 21.96 million (A$20.67 million), against a prospectus forecast of kina 12.60 million.
The result was boosted by a one-off kina 5.53 million abnormal gain, related to the conversion of share proceeds to kina, Orogen said.
